Senses.Explanation: To have a discerning eye: to be able to recognize, distinguish, or judge what an encounter puts forward. Danxia Tianran asks whether the person who fed a traveler has such an eye, and Muzhou Daoming asks the same about a donor after an unnamed participant returns from a meal. Fayan Wenyi explicitly tells an unnamed participant that his earlier question shows a discerning eye, then asks why he did not cover the exchange before the public assembly. Jiashan Shanhui gives the negative boundary: someone who depends on buddha-and-patriarch sayings as a model has not yet acquired the eye. Fayun Faxiu promises the eye if listeners can identify the color of the wind. Yuanwu Keqin asks those with the eye to judge whether Xuedou or the Buddha has exposed the other. Tiantong Hongzhi says an eye-equipped Chan participant will recognize and assent to his sequence of circle figures; Sanshan Lai says such a discerning guide departs as soon as the matter is raised. Mingjue Cong uses the forehead-eye expansion when he says the teaching seat should make each person discerning and impartial underfoot. Chan bends ordinary possession of sight into a public capacity that named speakers confer, question, demand, and test; it is not a physical-eye diagnosis and not automatic approval of every claim.
Senses.Note: Frozen-corpus concordance: 1,584 exact hits in 308 files and 304 independent works. The base form, the qualified correct-eye form, and the forehead-eye form belong to one discernment family here; the longer forms specify qualification or location but do not name different faculties. Nominal English ('one with a discerning eye') and verbal English ('to have a discerning eye') are grammatical renderings of the same property, not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 將飯與闍黎喫底人。還具眼也無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Danxia Tianran section. Danxia Tianran is the exact speaker asking whether the person who gave the traveling monk food has a discerning eye.
Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), Muzhou Daoming record. Muzhou Daoming is the exact speaker asking a monk returning from a meal whether the donor has a discerning eye.

Occurrences.Kwic: 眼曰：上座適來問底話，許你具眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), Bao'en Xuance section. The line explicitly names Fayan Wenyi as the exact speaker who tells the monk that his earlier question warrants calling him discerning.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若向佛祖邊學。此人未具眼在。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Jiashan Shanhui section. Jiashan Shanhui is the exact speaker saying that a person who learns by depending on the buddhas and patriarchs has not yet acquired a discerning eye.

The Full Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Fayun Faxiu Yuantong section. Fayun Faxiu is the exact speaker promising to call listeners discerning if they can identify the color of the wind in his public question.

Pointing at the Moon Record (指月錄), Diamond Sutra comments. The text explicitly introduces Yuanwu Keqin's comment; Yuanwu is the exact historical speaker asking those with a discerning eye to decide whether Xuedou or the Buddha has exposed the other.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若是具眼衲僧。必也相許。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Essentials from the Successive Patriarchs' Addresses (列祖提綱錄), explicitly introduced as Tiantong Hongzhi Zhengjue's bathing-the-Buddha hall address. Hongzhi is the exact speaker saying that a discerning Chan monk will necessarily recognize and assent to the displayed sequence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 具眼阿師纔聞舉著便掉臂而去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanshan Lai (三山來禪師語錄), restriction-period hall address. Sanshan Lai is the exact speaker saying that a discerning teacher leaves as soon as the matter is raised.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直令個個頂門具眼人人腳底無私
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mingjue Cong (明覺聰禪師語錄), opening hall address at Minzhong Monastery. Mingjue Cong is the exact speaker saying the teaching seat should make each person have a discerning forehead-eye and impartial footing.
